title: Sanitize five buggy kernels
brief: Fix five CUDA kernels that each hide one bug, then read what compute-sanitizer prints. The kernels are an out-of-bounds write, a shared-memory race, a missed __syncwarp, a divergent __syncthreads, and an uninitialized shared read. You also write a parser that turns recorded sanitizer reports into findings, and two pure-Python functions that find the racing reads and the out-of-bounds threads.
hints: Start with error_count. The report ends with 'ERROR SUMMARY: N errors', or '1 error' when N is 1. N counts every failing access, and the tool prints only the first few, so the number of findings is not N.

The report never names its tool. Infer it from the header line: Invalid ... is memcheck, Uninitialized ... is initcheck, Barrier error ... is synccheck, and a Potential RAW, WAR, or WAW hazard is racecheck.

Split the report into findings at the blank '=========' lines. A finding's 'at' line (memcheck, initcheck, synccheck) reads 'at <kernel>+0x<offset> in <file>:<line>'. A racecheck access line reads '<Write|Read> Thread (x,y,z) at 0x.. in <file>:<line>:<kernel>'. Skip the 'Host Frame' lines.
The kernel name stops at the first '(' or '<'. Remove a leading 'void ' first.
A racecheck header that says Warning is not an error in ERROR SUMMARY. is_clean counts it anyway, because the kernel is still racy.

shared_hazards: in phase k, thread t < d reads s[t + d], and that address was written in phase k - 1 by thread t + d. A barrier between the two phases ends the hazard. Count one hazard per (address, writer, reader).
barrier_arrivals: with an early return, the threads that arrive are those whose global index is below n. The count is clamped between 0 and block_dim.

Kernel 1: guard the read and the write with i < n. Kernel 2: add __syncthreads() inside the loop. Kernel 3: read into a register, __syncwarp(), write the register to shared memory, __syncwarp(). Kernel 4: remove the early return, load zero for a thread past the end, and guard only the store. Kernel 5: thread 0 loads tile[0] and thread B - 1 loads tile[B + 1], each with a bounds check.

The CUDA checks compile five modules with -lineinfo, which takes a few minutes the first time. Each module then runs under compute-sanitizer in a process of its own, with PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 so that memcheck sees every allocation exactly.
On a machine without a GPU or without compute-sanitizer the two CUDA checks are skipped. The seven checks that run anywhere still grade your parser and your reasoning.
